216	                "passes": passes, "n": len(runs), "threshold": threshold, "z": self.cfg.z, "round": round_,
217	            }) as sp:
218	                if decision is Decision.INCONCLUSIVE and capped:
219	                    verdict, flag = (Verdict.GOOD if passes / len(runs) >= threshold else Verdict.BAD), "low_confidence"
220	                elif decision is Decision.INCONCLUSIVE:
221	                    verdict, flag = None, None
222	                else:
223	                    verdict, flag = Verdict(decision.value), None
224	                sp.output({"decision": decision, "wilson": [low, high], "verdict": verdict, "flag": flag})
225	            step = self.ledger.get_step(run_id, kind, sha)
226	            self.ledger.set_decision(step["step_id"], verdict or Decision.INCONCLUSIVE, flag, low, high,
227	                                     len(runs), passes)
228	            self.log(f"  {sha[:10]} {gitops.subject(self.repo, sha)[:44]!r}: {passes}/{len(runs)} "
229	                     f"CI [{low:.2f}, {high:.2f}] vs t={threshold:.2f} → {decision}"
230	                     + (f" → {verdict} ({flag})" if flag else ""))
231	            if final:
232	                return verdict  # type: ignore[return-value]
233	            tasks, reps = plans[round_]
234	            kind = f"resample:{round_ + 1}"
235	            self.log(f"    resample {round_ + 1}: {len(tasks)} tasks × reps {reps.start}..{reps.stop - 1}")
236	            extra = self.evaluate(run_id, kind, sha, tasks, reps)
237	            if extra.skipped:  # cannot happen after a successful install, but stay safe
238	                return Verdict.SKIP
239	            runs += extra.runs
240	        raise AssertionError("unreachable")
241	
242	    # whole run -----------------------------------------------------------------
243	    def start(self) -> str:
244	        return self.ledger.create_run(str(self.repo), self.cfg.good_ref, self.cfg.bad_ref,
245	                                      suite_hash(list(self.cfg.task_ids)), self.cfg.to_json())
246	
247	    def run(self, run_id: str) -> Outcome:
248	        bad_sha = self.ledger.get_run(run_id)["bad_sha"] or gitops.resolve(self.repo, self.cfg.bad_ref)
249	        with tracing.run_context(run_id=run_id), tracing.span(
250	            "culprit_run", "WORKFLOW", commit_sha=bad_sha,
251	            input={"good": self.cfg.good_ref, "bad": self.cfg.bad_ref, "k": self.cfg.k},
252	        ) as sp:
253	            trace_id = tracing.current_trace_id()
254	            if trace_id:
255	                previous = self.ledger.get_artifact(run_id, "neatlogs_traces")
256	                self.ledger.put_artifact(run_id, "neatlogs_traces", f"{previous}\n{trace_id}" if previous else trace_id)
257	                self.log(f"neatlogs trace {trace_id}")
258	            try:
259	                outcome = self._run(run_id)
260	            except Exception as exc:
261	                self.ledger.finish_run(run_id, "error", None, None, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
262	                raise
263	            sp.output({"status": outcome.status, "summary": outcome.summary})
264	            return outcome
265	
266	    def _pin_suite(self, run_id: str) -> suite.PinnedSuite:
267	        """First run: snapshot the suite and record it. Resume: rebuild the recorded snapshot."""
268	        row = self.ledger.get_run(run_id)
269	        with tracing.span("pin_suite", "TOOL", input={"suite": self.cfg.suite, "suite_ref": self.cfg.suite_ref,
270	                                                      "recorded": row["suite_sha"]}) as sp:
271	            if row["suite_sha"]:
272	                pinned = suite.restore(self.repo, row["suite_source"], row["suite_sha"])
273	            else:
274	                pinned = suite.pin(self.repo, self.cfg.suite, self.cfg.suite_ref)
275	                self.ledger.set_suite(run_id, pinned.source, pinned.sha)
276	            sp.output({"source": pinned.source, "sha": pinned.sha})
277	        self.log(f"  suite pinned: {pinned.source} @ {pinned.sha[:12]}")
278	        return pinned
279	
280	    def _ensure_tasks(self, run_id: str, good: str) -> list[str]:
281	        if not self.cfg.task_ids:
282	            assert self.pinned is not None
283	            with tracing.span("discover_tasks", "TOOL", commit_sha=good, input={"suite": self.cfg.suite}) as sp:
284	                tasks = discover_tasks(self.pinned.path)
285	                sp.output({"tasks": tasks})
286	            self.cfg = replace(self.cfg, task_ids=tuple(tasks))
287	            self.ledger.update_config(run_id, suite_hash(tasks), self.cfg.to_json())
288	        return list(self.cfg.task_ids)
289	
290	    def _run(self, run_id: str) -> Outcome:
291	        cfg, repo = self.cfg, self.repo
292	        with tracing.span("git_rev_list", "TOOL", input={"good": cfg.good_ref, "bad": cfg.bad_ref}) as sp:
293	            good, bad = self._range(run_id)
294	            candidates = gitops.first_parent_range(repo, good, bad)
295	            sp.output({"good": good, "bad": bad, "candidates": candidates})
296	        if self.victim is not None:
297	            try:
298	                self.victim.require_key()  # e.g. a run started with Anthropic, resumed without the key
299	            except ProviderError as exc:
300	                return self._finish(run_id, "infra_error", None, f"Stopped: {exc}")
301	            self.log(f"  victim model: {self.victim.model} via {self.victim.name}")
302	        if not candidates:  # before the baselines, which are the most expensive part of a run
303	            return self._finish(run_id, "error", None, f"empty range: {cfg.good_ref}..{cfg.bad_ref} has no commits")
304	        tested: list[tuple[str, Verdict]] = []
305	        try:
306	            return self._bisect(run_id, good, bad, candidates, tested)
307	        except BudgetExceeded as exc:
308	            return self._budget_stop(run_id, exc, candidates, tested)
309	        except InfraError as exc:
310	            return self._finish(run_id, "infra_error", None,
311	                                f"Stopped: {exc}. Nothing was counted against the commit. Fix the cause, then "
312	                                f"`culprit resume {run_id}` continues where it stopped.")
313	
314	    def _range(self, run_id: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
315	        """Good and bad SHAs, resolved once; resume keeps them even if the refs have moved since."""
316	        row = self.ledger.get_run(run_id)
317	        if row["good_sha"] and row["bad_sha"]:
318	            return row["good_sha"], row["bad_sha"]
319	        good, bad = gitops.resolve(self.repo, self.cfg.good_ref), gitops.resolve(self.repo, self.cfg.bad_ref)
320	        self.ledger.set_range(run_id, good, bad)
321	        return good, bad
322	
323	    def _bisect(self, run_id: str, good: str, bad: str, candidates: list[str],
324	                tested: list[tuple[str, Verdict]]) -> Outcome:
325	        cfg, repo = self.cfg, self.repo
326	        self.pinned = self._pin_suite(run_id)
327	        tasks = self._ensure_tasks(run_id, good)
328	        self.log(f"run {run_id}: {len(candidates)} commits in {cfg.good_ref}..{cfg.bad_ref}, "
329	                 f"{len(tasks)} tasks × {cfg.k}")
330	
331	        base = Baselines(self.evaluate(run_id, "baseline", good, tasks, range(cfg.k)),
332	                         self.evaluate(run_id, "baseline", bad, tasks, range(cfg.k)))
333	        if base.good.skipped or base.bad.skipped:
334	            return self._finish(run_id, "error", None, "good or bad ref failed to install; cannot bisect")
335	        ci_good = wilson(base.good.passes, base.good.n, cfg.z)
336	        ci_bad = wilson(base.bad.passes, base.bad.n, cfg.z)
337	        self.log(f"  good {base.good.passes}/{base.good.n} CI [{ci_good[0]:.2f}, {ci_good[1]:.2f}]  "
338	                 f"bad {base.bad.passes}/{base.bad.n} CI [{ci_bad[0]:.2f}, {ci_bad[1]:.2f}]")
339	        p_value = fisher_one_sided(base.good.passes, base.good.n, base.bad.passes, base.bad.n)
340	        with tracing.span("regression_gate", "TOOL", input={
341	            "good": [base.good.passes, base.good.n], "bad": [base.bad.passes, base.bad.n], "alpha": cfg.gate_alpha,
342	        }) as sp:
343	            significant = base.good.rate > base.bad.rate and p_value < cfg.gate_alpha
344	            sp.output({"p_value": p_value, "significant": significant})
345	        self.log(f"  regression gate: one-sided Fisher p={p_value:.4f} (alpha {cfg.gate_alpha})")
346	        if not significant:
347	            return self._finish(run_id, "no_regression", None,
348	                                f"No significant regression to bisect: good {base.good.passes}/{base.good.n} vs "
349	                                f"bad {base.bad.passes}/{base.bad.n}, one-sided Fisher p={p_value:.4f} "
350	                                f"≥ {cfg.gate_alpha}")
351	        with tracing.span("select_discriminating_tasks", "TOOL", input={"size": cfg.discriminating_size}) as sp:
352	            ranked = self.ranked_tasks(base)
353	            subset = [t for t in ranked if base.drop(t) > 0]
354	            subset = subset[: cfg.discriminating_size] or ranked[: cfg.discriminating_size]
355	            sp.output({"tasks": subset, "ranked": ranked})
356	        self.log(f"  discriminating tasks: {', '.join(subset)}")
357	
358	        result = bisect(candidates, lambda sha: self.classify(run_id, sha, base, subset, ranked), tested)
359	        low_conf = [s["commit_sha"][:10] for s in self.ledger.steps(run_id) if s["flags"] == "low_confidence"]
360	        confidence = "95% Wilson" if not low_conf else f"low: point estimate decided {', '.join(low_conf)}"
361	        if result.first_bad is None:
362	            summary = f"Culprit is one of {len(result.suspects)} commits (skipped commits hide the boundary): " + \
363	                ", ".join(s[:10] for s in result.suspects)
364	            return self._finish(run_id, "ambiguous", result, summary, confidence)
365	
366	        with tracing.span("entire_checkpoint_explain", "TOOL", commit_sha=result.first_bad,
367	                          input={"sha": result.first_bad}) as sp:
368	            intent = commit_intent(repo, result.first_bad)
369	            sp.output({"available": intent.available, "checkpoint_id": intent.checkpoint_id,
370	                       "source": intent.source, "lines_removed": intent.lines_removed})
371	        self.ledger.put_artifact(run_id, "intent", intent.text)
372	        self.ledger.put_artifact(run_id, "diff", gitops.diff(repo, result.first_bad))
373	        self.log(f"  intent source: {intent.source}; leakage filter removed {intent.lines_removed} lines")
374	        summary = f"Culprit: {result.first_bad} {gitops.subject(repo, result.first_bad)!r} (confidence: {confidence})"
375	        return self._finish(run_id, "found", result, summary, confidence)
376	
377	    def ranked_tasks(self, base: Baselines) -> list[str]:
378	        """Tasks ranked by pass-rate drop from good to bad (deterministic part of the Task Selector)."""
379	        g, b = base.good.task_rates(), base.bad.task_rates()
380	        return [t for _, t in sorted(((g[t] - b.get(t, 0.0), t) for t in g), key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))]
381	
382	    def _budget_stop(self, run_id: str, exc: BudgetExceeded, candidates: list[str],
383	                     tested: list[tuple[str, Verdict]]) -> Outcome:
384	        lo, hi = bounds(candidates, tested)
385	        suspects = candidates[lo + 1 : hi + 1]
386	        summary = (f"Stopped: {exc}. Best current range: {len(suspects)} commits "
387	                   f"{suspects[0][:10]}..{suspects[-1][:10]}; tested {len(tested)} so far. "
388	                   f"Resume with `culprit resume {run_id} --budget-usd <higher>` to continue.")
389	        result = BisectResult(first_bad=None, suspects=suspects, tested=tested)
390	        return self._finish(run_id, "budget_exceeded", result, summary)
391	
392	    def _finish(self, run_id: str, status: str, result: BisectResult | None, summary: str,
393	                confidence: str | None = None) -> Outcome:
394	        self.ledger.finish_run(run_id, status, result.first_bad if result else None, confidence, summary)
395	        self.log(summary)
396	        return Outcome(run_id, status, result, summary)

398	
399	Every write is idempotent: steps are unique per (run_id, kind, commit_sha) and task runs per
400	(step_id, task_id, repetition). Resume works by replaying the deterministic controller, which
401	reuses any recorded step or task run instead of executing it again.
402	"""

488	def _now() -> str:
489	    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")

491	
492	@dataclass(frozen=True)
493	class TaskRun:
494	    task_id: str
495	    repetition: int
496	    passed: bool
497	    cost_usd: float | None
498	    latency_ms: float | None
499	    tokens_in: int | None
500	    tokens_out: int | None
501	    trace_id: str | None
502	    error: str | None = None

504	
505	class Ledger:
506	    def __init__(self, path: Path):
507	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
508	        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None)
509	        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
510	        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
511	        self.conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
512	        columns = {r["name"] for r in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(steps)")}
513	        if "flags" not in columns:  # ledgers created before M2
514	            self.conn.execute("ALTER TABLE steps ADD COLUMN flags TEXT")
515	        run_columns = {r["name"] for r in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(runs)")}
516	        # ledgers created before the suite was pinned, or before refs were resolved once per run
517	        for column in ("suite_source", "suite_sha", "good_sha", "bad_sha"):
518	            if column not in run_columns:
519	                self.conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE runs ADD COLUMN {column} TEXT")
520	
521	    @contextmanager
522	    def _tx(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
523	        self.conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
524	        try:
525	            yield self.conn
526	        except BaseException:
527	            self.conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
528	            raise
529	        self.conn.execute("COMMIT")

531	    # runs -----------------------------------------------------------------
532	    def create_run(self, repo: str, good: str, bad: str, suite_hash: str, config_json: str) -> str:
533	        run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
534	        with self._tx() as c:
535	            c.execute(
536	                "INSERT INTO runs (run_id, repo, good_ref, bad_ref, suite_hash, config_json, status, started_at)"
537	                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'running', ?)",
538	                (run_id, repo, good, bad, suite_hash, config_json, _now()),
539	            )
540	        return run_id
541	
542	    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row:
543	        row = self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM runs WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,)).fetchone()
544	        if row is None:
545	            raise KeyError(f"unknown run_id {run_id}")
546	        return row
547	
548	    def update_config(self, run_id: str, suite_hash: str, config_json: str) -> None:
549	        with self._tx() as c:

551	                      (suite_hash, config_json, run_id))

553	    def set_suite(self, run_id: str, source: str, sha: str) -> None:

557	    def set_range(self, run_id: str, good_sha: str, bad_sha: str) -> None:

562	        self, run_id: str, status: str, culprit_sha: str | None, confidence: str | None, summary: str
563	    ) -> None:

565	            c.execute(
566	                "UPDATE runs SET status = ?, finished_at = ?, culprit_sha = ?, confidence = ?, summary = ?,"
567	                " total_cost_usd = ? WHERE run_id = ?",
568	                (status, _now(), culprit_sha, confidence, summary, self.run_cost(run_id), run_id),
569	            )

571	    def run_cost(self, run_id: str) -> float:
572	        victim = self.conn.execute(
573	            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.cost_usd), 0) FROM task_runs t JOIN steps s USING (step_id) WHERE s.run_id = ?",
574	            (run_id,),
575	        ).fetchone()[0]
576	        llm = self.conn.execute(
577	            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_calls WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,)
578	        ).fetchone()[0]
579	        return float(victim) + float(llm)

582	        """Cost across every run in this ledger, for the global (event-wide) cap."""
583	        victim = self.conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM task_runs").fetchone()[0]
584	        llm = self.conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_calls").fetchone()[0]
585	        return float(victim) + float(llm)

700	def wilson(passes: int, n: int, z: float = 1.96) -> tuple[float, float]:
701	    """95% (by default) Wilson score interval for `passes` successes in `n` trials."""
702	    if n <= 0:
703	        return 0.0, 1.0
704	    if not 0 <= passes <= n:
705	        raise ValueError(f"passes={passes} outside [0, {n}]")
706	    p = passes / n
707	    z2 = z * z
708	    denom = 1 + z2 / n
709	    centre = (p + z2 / (2 * n)) / denom
710	    half = z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z2 / (4 * n * n)) / denom
711	    return max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half)

716	    if low >= threshold:

718	    if high <= threshold:

729	
730	    Checking whether two 95% intervals overlap is far stricter than a 5% test: 57/60 vs 48/60

732	    test on the same 2×2 table: P(good would score at least `good_passes` if both had one rate).

735	    denom = math.comb(n, total_pass)
736	    upper = min(good_n, total_pass)

def count_task_runs(ledger) -> int:
    return ledger.conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task_runs").fetchone()[0]


def test_finds_culprit_and_resume_reuses_work(env):
    from culprit.ledger import Ledger

    repo, db, orchestrator, config = env
    ledger = Ledger(db)
    cfg = config.Config(repo=str(repo), good_ref="good-v1.0", bad_ref="main")
    orch = orchestrator.Orchestrator(ledger, cfg, log=lambda _: None)
    run_id = orch.start()
    outcome = orch.run(run_id)

    expected = subprocess.check_output(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "log", "--format=%H", "--grep=speed up tool handling"], text=True
    ).strip()
    assert outcome.status == "found"
    assert outcome.result.first_bad == expected
    assert any(v == "SKIP" for _, v in outcome.result.tested)

    # Simulate a kill mid-step: forget one task run and mark the run unfinished.
    total = count_task_runs(ledger)
    ledger.conn.execute("DELETE FROM task_runs WHERE id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM task_runs)")
    ledger.conn.execute("UPDATE runs SET status = 'running' WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,))

    resumed = orchestrator.Orchestrator(
        ledger, config.Config.from_json(ledger.get_run(run_id)["config_json"]), log=lambda _: None
    ).run(run_id)
    assert resumed.result.first_bad == outcome.result.first_bad
    assert count_task_runs(ledger) == total  # only the forgotten run was re-executed

def _tokens(raw: Any) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
    if isinstance(raw, Mapping):
        tin = raw.get("in", raw.get("input", raw.get("input_tokens", raw.get("prompt_tokens"))))
        tout = raw.get("out", raw.get("output", raw.get("output_tokens", raw.get("completion_tokens"))))

# A victim run that failed for one of these reasons says nothing about the commit under test, so
# it must never count as a failed task. Transient errors are retried; fatal ones stop the run.
TRANSIENT_ERROR = re.compile(
    r"RateLimitError|APIConnectionError|APITimeoutError|InternalServerError|OverloadedError|"
    r"ServiceUnavailableError|overloaded_error|rate_limit_error|Error code: (?:429|5\d\d)|"
    r"^timeout after \d+s$|eval runner printed no JSON"
)
FATAL_ERROR = re.compile(
    r"AuthenticationError|PermissionDeniedError|ConfigError|credit balance|Could not resolve authentication|"
    r"NotFoundError: Error code: 404 .*model"
)


def infra_failure(tr: TaskRun) -> str | None:
    """'transient' or 'fatal' when the run failed for infrastructure reasons, else None."""
    if tr.passed or not tr.error:
        return None
    if FATAL_ERROR.search(tr.error):
        return "fatal"
    if TRANSIENT_ERROR.search(tr.error):
        return "transient"
    return None


def run_task(
    worktree: Path, base_env: Mapping[str, str], eval_module: str, task_id: str, repetition: int,
    *, run_id: str, commit_sha: str, timeout_s: int,
) -> TaskRun:
    env = dict(base_env) | {
        "CULPRIT_RUN_ID": run_id,
        "COMMIT_SHA": commit_sha,
        "TASK_ID": task_id,
        "REPETITION": str(repetition),
    }
    cmd = [str(python_of(worktree)), "-m", eval_module, "--task", task_id, "--seed", str(repetition)]
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=worktree, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return TaskRun(task_id, repetition, False, None, timeout_s * 1000.0, None, None, None,
                       f"timeout after {timeout_s}s")
    wall_ms = (time.monotonic() - started) * 1000.0
    try:
        out = _parse_output(proc.stdout)
    except ValueError as exc:
        tail = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout)[-400:]
        return TaskRun(task_id, repetition, False, None, wall_ms, None, None, None,
                       f"exit {proc.returncode}: {exc}: {tail}")
    tin, tout = _tokens(out.get("tokens"))
    # `latency_ms` is taken as-is; a bare `latency` is the runner's seconds value.
    if out.get("latency_ms") is not None:
        latency_ms = float(out["latency_ms"])
    elif out.get("latency") is not None:
        latency_ms = float(out["latency"]) * 1000.0
    else:
        latency_ms = wall_ms
    return TaskRun(
        task_id=task_id,
        repetition=repetition,
        passed=bool(out.get("passed")),
        cost_usd=None if out.get("cost") is None else float(out["cost"]),
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        tokens_in=tin,
        tokens_out=tout,
        trace_id=out.get("trace_id"),
        error=out.get("error"),
    )

"""Reuse baseline task runs from earlier runs in the ledger (v2 efficiency).

A victim task run is fully determined by what it ran: the commit, the pinned suite, the victim
provider and model, the eval runner, and the repetition (which is the seed). So a baseline measured
at a commit in one run is equally valid in any later run that matches all of those, and `k` too,
as the run key asks. Matching rows are copied into the new run's step with their origin
(`reused_from_run`, `reused_from_id`), so every number in the new run stays auditable, and they
are not counted as spend a second time.

Only original measurements are copied (never a row that was itself reused), so provenance always
points at the run that paid for the result.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter

from culprit.config import Config
from culprit.ledger import Ledger

ARTIFACT = "baseline_reuse"

# Earlier baseline task runs at `commit_sha` whose run matches the reuse key. The oldest original
# measurement wins, so repeated reuse keeps pointing at the same source.
_SOURCES = """
SELECT t.id, t.task_id, t.repetition, s.run_id
FROM task_runs t
JOIN steps s USING (step_id)
JOIN runs r ON r.run_id = s.run_id
WHERE s.commit_sha = :sha
  AND s.kind LIKE 'baseline%'
  AND s.run_id != :run_id
  AND t.reused_from_run IS NULL
  AND r.suite_sha = :suite_sha
  AND json_extract(r.config_json, '$.victim_provider') = :provider
  AND json_extract(r.config_json, '$.victim_model') = :model
  AND json_extract(r.config_json, '$.eval_module') = :eval_module
  AND json_extract(r.config_json, '$.k') = :k
ORDER BY t.id
"""


def import_runs(ledger: Ledger, cfg: Config, run_id: str, kind: str, sha: str,
                items: list[tuple[str, int]]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Copy matching earlier results for `items` (task, repetition) into this run's step.

    Returns {source run_id: rows copied}. Does nothing for a run without a pinned suite, or for a
    step that already holds a result (resume never replaces a recorded run).
    """
    suite_sha = ledger.get_run(run_id)["suite_sha"]
    if not (cfg.reuse_baselines and suite_sha and items):
        return {}
    wanted = set(items)
    sources: dict[tuple[str, int], tuple[int, str]] = {}
    for row in ledger.conn.execute(_SOURCES, {
        "sha": sha, "run_id": run_id, "suite_sha": suite_sha, "provider": cfg.victim_provider,
        "model": cfg.victim_model, "eval_module": cfg.eval_module, "k": cfg.k,
    }):
        key = (row["task_id"], row["repetition"])
        if key in wanted and key not in sources:
            sources[key] = (row["id"], row["run_id"])
    if not sources:
        return {}
    step_id = ledger.open_step(run_id, kind, sha)
    done = ledger.task_runs(step_id)
    copied: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for key, (source_id, source_run) in sorted(sources.items()):
        if key not in done and ledger.copy_task_run(step_id, source_id, source_run):
            copied[source_run] += 1
    if copied:
        _record(ledger, run_id, kind, sha, copied)
    return dict(copied)


def _record(ledger: Ledger, run_id: str, kind: str, sha: str, copied: Counter[str]) -> None:
    """Per-run provenance summary: {"<kind>:<sha>": {source run_id: rows}} in artifact `baseline_reuse`."""
    previous = ledger.get_artifact(run_id, ARTIFACT)
    summary = json.loads(previous) if previous else {}
    entry = summary.setdefault(f"{kind}:{sha}", {})
    for source, n in copied.items():
        entry[source] = entry.get(source, 0) + n
    ledger.put_artifact(run_id, ARTIFACT, json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True))


def provenance(ledger: Ledger, run_id: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
    text = ledger.get_artifact(run_id, ARTIFACT)
    return json.loads(text) if text else {}

"""Measure both ends of the range (v2: staged and reused).

v1 ran every task × k on the good and the bad commit: 26 tasks × 3 × 2 = 156 victim runs, the most
expensive part of a run. v2 does it in two stages:

1. **Screen**: every task × 1 (repetition 0) on both ends (step kind `baseline`).
2. **Full k**: repetitions 1..k-1, on both ends, only for tasks that did not pass on both ends in
   the screen (step kind `baseline:full`). Those are the tasks that differ, and the ones that may be
   flaky or broken on both sides. A task that passed once on each end gets no more runs.

Both ends always run the same (task, repetition) set, so the regression gate compares like with
like, and it uses exactly the runs that were made: n is the real count, not tasks × k. The
selection rule is symmetric in good and bad (swap the labels and the same tasks are chosen), so
under "no regression" it can't favour one side. It can miss a task that drops from good to bad but
happened to pass once on the bad end; the other dropped tasks still carry the signal.

Before each stage, results already measured for the same commit in an earlier matching run are
copied in (culprit.reuse), so only the gaps run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from culprit import reuse, tracing
from culprit.stats import wilson

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from culprit.orchestrator import Baselines, Orchestrator, StepResult

SCREEN = "baseline"
FULL = "baseline:full"


def screen_failures(good: StepResult, bad: StepResult) -> list[str]:
    """Tasks that did not pass on both ends of the screen: these get the full k."""
    g, b = good.task_rates(), bad.task_rates()
    return sorted(t for t in g if not (g[t] == 1.0 and b.get(t, 0.0) == 1.0))


def _measure(orch: Orchestrator, run_id: str, kind: str, sha: str, tasks: list[str], reps: range) -> StepResult:
    copied = reuse.import_runs(orch.ledger, orch.cfg, run_id, kind, sha, [(t, r) for t in tasks for r in reps])
    if copied:
        with tracing.span("reuse_baseline", "TOOL", commit_sha=sha, input={"kind": kind}) as sp:
            sp.output({"copied_from": copied})
        orch.log(f"  {sha[:10]} {kind}: reused " + ", ".join(f"{n} runs from {src}" for src, n in copied.items()))
    return orch.evaluate(run_id, kind, sha, tasks, reps)


def measure(orch: Orchestrator, run_id: str, good: str, bad: str, tasks: list[str]) -> Baselines:
    from culprit.orchestrator import Baselines, StepResult

    k = orch.cfg.k
    if not orch.cfg.staged_baseline or k <= 1:
        return Baselines(_measure(orch, run_id, SCREEN, good, tasks, range(k)),
                         _measure(orch, run_id, SCREEN, bad, tasks, range(k)))
    g1 = _measure(orch, run_id, SCREEN, good, tasks, range(1))
    b1 = _measure(orch, run_id, SCREEN, bad, tasks, range(1))
    if g1.skipped or b1.skipped:
        return Baselines(g1, b1)
    deep = screen_failures(g1, b1)
    with tracing.span("baseline_screen", "TOOL", input={"tasks": len(tasks), "k": k}) as sp:
        sp.output({"full_k": deep, "screen": [[g1.passes, g1.n], [b1.passes, b1.n]]})
    orch.log(f"  screen ×1: good {g1.passes}/{g1.n}, bad {b1.passes}/{b1.n}; full k={k} on {len(deep)} tasks")
    if not deep:
        return Baselines(g1, b1)
    g2 = _measure(orch, run_id, FULL, good, deep, range(1, k))
    b2 = _measure(orch, run_id, FULL, bad, deep, range(1, k))
    good_all, bad_all = StepResult(good, False, g1.runs + g2.runs), StepResult(bad, False, b1.runs + b2.runs)
    for step_kind, sha, res in ((FULL, good, good_all), (FULL, bad, bad_all)):
        # The full-k step row carries the whole baseline for that end (screen + full), like a resample.
        row = orch.ledger.get_step(run_id, step_kind, sha)
        low, high = wilson(res.passes, res.n, orch.cfg.z)
        orch.ledger.set_decision(row["step_id"], row["decision"] or "", row["flags"], low, high, res.n, res.passes)
    return Baselines(good_all, bad_all)

def build(path: Path, commits: int, breaks_at: int, unbuildable_at: int | None, noisy_from: int | None = None,
          noisy_pass: float = 0.75, late_task: bool = False) -> Path:
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)

    (pkg / "agent.py").write_text(AGENT.format(p=0.95))
    (pkg / "eval.py").write_text(EVAL.format())
    (path / "pyproject.toml").write_text(PYPROJECT.format(deps=""))
    (path / ".gitignore").write_text(".venv/\n")
    evals = path / "evals"
    evals.mkdir()
    for i in range(1, 11):
        (evals / f"t{i:02d}.json").write_text('{"message": "refund please"}\n')
    sh(path, "uv", "lock", "-q")
    commit(path, "initial agent")
    sh(path, "git", "tag", "good-v1.0")

    notes = path / "NOTES.md"
    for n in range(1, commits + 1):
        # The dependency pin and the agent's pass rate are independent files, so every change due at
        # commit n is applied; one never displaces another (e.g. the pin revert and a noisy commit).
        changes = []
        if unbuildable_at is not None and n == unbuildable_at:
            (path / "pyproject.toml").write_text(PYPROJECT.format(deps='"requests==99.99.99"'))
            changes.append("pin requests")
        elif unbuildable_at is not None and n == unbuildable_at + 1:
            (path / "pyproject.toml").write_text(PYPROJECT.format(deps=""))
            changes.append("revert requests pin")
        if n == breaks_at:
            (pkg / "agent.py").write_text(AGENT.format(p=0.05))
            changes.append("speed up tool handling")
        elif noisy_from is not None and n == noisy_from:
            (pkg / "agent.py").write_text(AGENT.format(p=noisy_pass))
            changes.append("tune tool timeouts")
        if late_task and n == commits:
            (evals / "t11.json").write_text('{"message": "refund the second order"}\n')
            changes.append("evals: add t11")
        if not changes:
            with notes.open("a") as f:
                f.write(f"- maintenance note {n}\n")
            changes.append(f"docs: maintenance note {n}")
        commit(path, "; ".join(changes))
    return path


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()

    p.add_argument("--breaks-at", type=int, default=10)

"""Per-run cost accounting from the ledger: `culprit export-costs` and the v1→v2 comparison.

A victim run "made" by a run is a task run it executed and paid for. Task runs copied from an
earlier run (culprit.reuse) are counted separately as `reused_runs` and cost nothing here; their
cost stays with the run that measured them, so summing `cost_usd` over runs never double-counts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, fields
from datetime import datetime
from typing import TextIO

from culprit.ledger import Ledger


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunCosts:
    run_id: str
    repo: str
    good_ref: str
    bad_ref: str
    status: str
    victim_provider: str
    victim_model: str
    k: int
    victim_runs: int  # executed by this run
    baseline_runs: int  # of victim_runs, measuring the two ends
    bisect_runs: int  # of victim_runs, bisect steps and resamples
    reused_runs: int  # copied from earlier runs, not executed
    victim_cost_usd: float
    llm_cost_usd: float
    cost_usd: float
    cost_per_victim_run_usd: float | None
    wall_time_s: float | None  # started → finished; includes any pause before a resume
    started_at: str
    finished_at: str | None
    culprit_sha: str | None


_COUNTS = """
SELECT
  COALESCE(SUM(t.reused_from_run IS NULL), 0) AS executed,
  COALESCE(SUM(t.reused_from_run IS NULL AND s.kind LIKE 'baseline%'), 0) AS baseline,
  COALESCE(SUM(t.reused_from_run IS NOT NULL), 0) AS reused,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.reused_from_run IS NULL THEN t.cost_usd END), 0) AS cost
FROM task_runs t JOIN steps s USING (step_id) WHERE s.run_id = ?
"""


def _wall_time(started: str, finished: str | None) -> float | None:
    if not finished:
        return None
    return (datetime.fromisoformat(finished) - datetime.fromisoformat(started)).total_seconds()


def run_costs(ledger: Ledger, run_id: str) -> RunCosts:
    row = ledger.get_run(run_id)
    cfg = json.loads(row["config_json"])
    c = ledger.conn.execute(_COUNTS, (run_id,)).fetchone()
    llm = float(ledger.conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_calls WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,)).fetchone()[0])
    victim_cost = float(c["cost"])
    executed = int(c["executed"])
    return RunCosts(
        run_id=run_id, repo=row["repo"], good_ref=row["good_ref"], bad_ref=row["bad_ref"], status=row["status"],
        victim_provider=cfg.get("victim_provider", ""), victim_model=cfg.get("victim_model", ""),
        k=int(cfg.get("k", 0)), victim_runs=executed, baseline_runs=int(c["baseline"]),
        bisect_runs=executed - int(c["baseline"]), reused_runs=int(c["reused"]),
        victim_cost_usd=round(victim_cost, 6), llm_cost_usd=round(llm, 6), cost_usd=round(victim_cost + llm, 6),
        cost_per_victim_run_usd=round(victim_cost / executed, 6) if executed else None,
        wall_time_s=_wall_time(row["started_at"], row["finished_at"]),
        started_at=row["started_at"], finished_at=row["finished_at"], culprit_sha=row["culprit_sha"],
    )


def all_runs(ledger: Ledger) -> list[RunCosts]:
    ids = [r[0] for r in ledger.conn.execute("SELECT run_id FROM runs ORDER BY started_at, run_id")]
    return [run_costs(ledger, run_id) for run_id in ids]


def write_csv(rows: list[RunCosts], out: TextIO) -> None:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(out, fieldnames=[f.name for f in fields(RunCosts)], lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writeheader()
    for r in rows:
        writer.writerow({k: "" if v is None else v for k, v in asdict(r).items()})

import importlib
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"))
from make_victim import build  # noqa: E402

from culprit.ledger import Ledger, TaskRun  # noqa: E402

V1 = {"reuse_baselines": False, "staged_baseline": False}


@pytest.fixture()
def mods(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("CULPRIT_STATE_DIR", str(tmp_path / "state"))
    import culprit.baseline
    import culprit.config
    import culprit.orchestrator
    import culprit.sandbox
    import culprit.suite

    for mod in (culprit.config, culprit.sandbox, culprit.suite, culprit.orchestrator):
        importlib.reload(mod)
    return culprit.orchestrator, culprit.config


@pytest.fixture()
def repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    return build(tmp_path / "victim", commits=14, breaks_at=10, unbuildable_at=7)


def culprit_sha(repo: Path) -> str:
    return subprocess.check_output(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "log", "--format=%H", "--grep=speed up tool handling"], text=True
    ).strip()


def run(mods, repo: Path, db: Path, log: list[str] | None = None, **overrides):
    orchestrator, config = mods
    fields = {"good_ref": "good-v1.0", "bad_ref": "main", "victim_provider": "anthropic",
              "victim_model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", **overrides}
    cfg = config.Config(repo=str(repo), **fields)
    orch = orchestrator.Orchestrator(Ledger(db), cfg, log=(log.append if log is not None else lambda _: None))
    orch.victim = None  # the fixture needs no key; the model is only part of the reuse key
    run_id = orch.start()
    return orch, run_id, orch.run(run_id)


def baseline_rows(ledger: Ledger, run_id: str, sha: str, executed_only: bool = False) -> list:
    return ledger.conn.execute(
        "SELECT t.* FROM task_runs t JOIN steps s USING (step_id) WHERE s.run_id = ? AND s.commit_sha = ?"
        " AND s.kind LIKE 'baseline%'" + (" AND t.reused_from_run IS NULL" if executed_only else ""),
        (run_id, sha),
    ).fetchall()


# Staged baseline -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_screen_sends_only_tasks_that_did_not_pass_on_both_ends_to_full_k(mods):
    orchestrator, _ = mods
    from culprit.baseline import screen_failures

    def step(spec):
        return orchestrator.StepResult("x", False, [TaskRun(t, 0, p, None, None, None, None, None) for t, p in spec])

    good = step([("a", True), ("b", True), ("c", False), ("d", True)])
    bad = step([("a", True), ("b", False), ("c", False), ("d", True)])
    assert screen_failures(good, bad) == ["b", "c"]  # b differs; c fails on both (flaky or broken)


def test_v1_baseline_runs_every_task_k_times(mods, repo: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    orch, run_id, outcome = run(mods, repo, tmp_path / "l.sqlite", **V1)
    assert outcome.result.first_bad == culprit_sha(repo)
    good, bad = orch.ledger.get_run(run_id)["good_sha"], orch.ledger.get_run(run_id)["bad_sha"]
    assert len(baseline_rows(orch.ledger, run_id, good)) == len(baseline_rows(orch.ledger, run_id, bad)) == 30


def test_staged_baseline_finds_the_same_culprit_with_fewer_runs(mods, repo: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    log: list[str] = []
    orch, run_id, outcome = run(mods, repo, tmp_path / "l.sqlite", log=log)
    assert outcome.status == "found"
    assert outcome.result.first_bad == culprit_sha(repo)
    row = orch.ledger.get_run(run_id)

"""Victim runs per bisect, v1 vs v2, on the free fixture victim (no LLM, no network, $0).

    uv run python scripts/v2_efficiency.py [--out evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md]

For each scenario it builds a fixture repo and runs:
  v1          every task × k on both ends (reuse and staging off)
  v2          staged baseline, fresh ledger (nothing to reuse)
  v2 branch2  a second bad branch from the same good ref, same ledger: the good end is reused
  v2 rerun    the same range again, same ledger: both ends are reused
and checks every run names the planted commit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures"))

SCENARIOS = [  # (name, build kwargs)
    ("break #10 of 14, unbuildable #7", {"commits": 14, "breaks_at": 10, "unbuildable_at": 7}),
    ("break #4 of 14", {"commits": 14, "breaks_at": 4, "unbuildable_at": None}),
    ("break #12 of 16, unbuildable #8", {"commits": 16, "breaks_at": 12, "unbuildable_at": 8}),
    ("break #10 of 14, noisy #9 (p=0.6)", {"commits": 14, "breaks_at": 10, "unbuildable_at": 7,
                                           "noisy_from": 9, "noisy_pass": 0.6}),
]
V1 = {"reuse_baselines": False, "staged_baseline": False}


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="also write the markdown table here")
    a = p.parse_args()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        os.environ["CULPRIT_STATE_DIR"] = str(Path(tmp) / "state")
        from make_victim import build

        from culprit.config import Config
        from culprit.costs import run_costs
        from culprit.ledger import Ledger
        from culprit.orchestrator import Orchestrator

        def run(repo: Path, db: Path, bad: str = "main", **overrides):
            cfg = Config(repo=str(repo), good_ref="good-v1.0", bad_ref=bad, victim_provider="fixture",
                         victim_model="fixture", **overrides)
            orch = Orchestrator(Ledger(db), cfg, log=lambda _: None)
            orch.victim = None
            run_id = orch.start()
            outcome = orch.run(run_id)
            return run_costs(orch.ledger, run_id), outcome

        lines = ["| Scenario | Run | Baseline runs | Bisect runs | **Victim runs** | Reused | vs v1 | Culprit |",
                 "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|"]
        totals: dict[str, int] = {}
        for i, (name, kwargs) in enumerate(SCENARIOS):
            repo = build(Path(tmp) / f"victim{i}", **kwargs)
            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "branch", "branch2", "main~1"], check=True)
            truth = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(repo), "log", "--format=%H",
                                             "--grep=speed up tool handling"], text=True).strip()
            v1_db, v2_db = Path(tmp) / f"v1-{i}.sqlite", Path(tmp) / f"v2-{i}.sqlite"
            rows = [("v1", *run(repo, v1_db, **V1)),
                    ("v2", *run(repo, v2_db)),
                    ("v2 branch2 (good reused)", *run(repo, v2_db, bad="branch2")),
                    ("v2 rerun (both reused)", *run(repo, v2_db))]
            base = rows[0][1].victim_runs
            for label, c, outcome in rows:
                totals[label] = totals.get(label, 0) + c.victim_runs
                ok = "✓" if outcome.result and outcome.result.first_bad == truth else f"✗ {outcome.status}"
                lines.append(f"| {name} | {label} | {c.baseline_runs} | {c.bisect_runs} | **{c.victim_runs}** | "
                             f"{c.reused_runs} | {c.victim_runs / base - 1:+.0%} | {ok} |")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("| Total over scenarios | Victim runs | vs v1 |")
        lines.append("|---|---:|---:|")
        for label, n in totals.items():
            lines.append(f"| {label} | {n} | {n / totals['v1'] - 1:+.0%} |")
    table = "\n".join(lines)
    print(table)
    if a.out:
        a.out.write_text(table + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


class GitError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def git(repo: Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise GitError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def resolve(repo: Path, ref: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{ref}^{{commit}}").strip()


def first_parent_range(repo: Path, good: str, bad: str) -> list[str]:
    """Commits after `good` up to and including `bad`, oldest first, first-parent only."""
    out = git(repo, "rev-list", "--first-parent", "--reverse", f"{good}..{bad}")
    return [line for line in out.splitlines() if line]


def subject(repo: Path, sha: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "log", "-1", "--format=%s", sha).strip()


def message(repo: Path, sha: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "log", "-1", "--format=%B", sha).strip()


def diff(repo: Path, sha: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "show", "--format=", "--patch", "--no-color", sha)

# cfo.ai inputs: Culprit unit economics and pricing hypotheses

Written 2026-10-10. This file gathers the numbers to type into cfo.ai by hand. Every figure is
marked **measured** (from a run's ledger or the build log), **projected** (derived from measured
numbers with a stated assumption) or **assumption**. Pricing scenarios A, B and C are
**hypotheses**: no customer has seen or validated any of them.

To refresh the measured inputs from the ledger:

```bash
uv run culprit export-costs --format csv --out business/runs.csv   # per run: cost, victim runs, wall time
```

## 1. Measured

| Input | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Real bisect, `hist/b`, GLM 5.3 victim (v1) | 240 victim runs, **$0.60**, 12.5 min | run `ff50e3620fdd` (hackathon.md) |
| … of which baseline / bisect | 156 / 84 runs | same run |
| Cost per victim run, GLM 5.3 | $0.0025 | $0.60 / 240 |
| Cost per victim run, Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $0.0163 | RefundDesk baseline, 78 runs for $1.27, at $2/$10 per MTok |
| Culprit's own LLM cost per bisect | $0 | no Culprit LLM stage runs in `culprit run` yet |
| v1 → v2 victim runs per bisect, fixture | −16% (staging alone), −34% (good end reused), −47% (both ends reused) | `evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md` |

## 2. Projected (cost of goods per bisect)

The v2 run counts are a projection for `hist/b` (see `evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md`): 164 runs
with a staged baseline, 124 when the good end is reused. Compute is an **assumption** of $0.04 per
bisect: one 4-vCPU runner at about $0.17/hour for about 12.5 minutes.

| Victim model | v1 (240 runs) | v2 (164 runs) | v2 + good reused (124 runs) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $3.95 | $2.71 | $2.06 |
| GLM 5.3 | $0.64 | $0.45 | $0.35 |

These include the $0.04 compute. They exclude fixed costs (hosting, neatlogs plan, support), which
cfo.ai should take as separate monthly lines; we have no measured values for them.

## 3. Pricing scenarios (hypotheses)

Bisects per repo per month is unknown. The tables use 10 and 30 as **assumptions**.

### A. Flat subscription per repo, Culprit pays the model

- Starter: **$49/repo/month**, 10 bisects included.
- Team: **$199/repo/month**, 30 bisects included.

| Plan | Model | COGS / month | Gross margin |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Starter (10) | Sonnet, v1 | $39.48 | 19% |
| Starter (10) | Sonnet, v2 | $27.10 | 45% |
| Starter (10) | GLM, v2 | $4.50 | 91% |
| Team (30) | Sonnet, v1 | $118.43 | 40% |
| Team (30) | Sonnet, v2 | $81.31 | 59% |
| Team (30) | GLM, v2 | $13.50 | 93% |

Risk: margin depends on the customer's victim model and on usage. A cap on included bisects is needed.

### B. Bring your own key, plus a platform fee

The customer's own model key pays for victim runs (about $2.67 per bisect on Sonnet 5.5, v2). Culprit charges
**$99/repo/month**.

| Bisects / month | Culprit COGS (compute only) | Gross margin |
|---|---:|---:|
| 10 | $0.40 | 99.6% |
| 30 | $1.20 | 98.8% |
| 100 | $4.00 | 96.0% |

Risk: there's no model-cost exposure, but the customer sees two bills. v2's efficiency lowers *their*
bill, not ours.

### C. Metered per bisect, Culprit pays the model

Charge **$5 per completed bisect**. A run that ends as `no_regression` or `budget_exceeded` costs less,
and charging for it is an open question.

| Model / version | COGS per bisect | Gross margin at $5 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sonnet 5.5, v1 | $3.95 | 21% |
| Sonnet 5.5, v2 | $2.71 | 46% |
| GLM 5.3, v1 | $0.64 | 87% |
| GLM 5.3, v2 | $0.45 | 91% |

This is the scenario where v2's efficiency matters most: on Sonnet it roughly doubles the margin
(21% → 46%).

## 4. Still to measure

- A real v2 run on `hist/b`, to replace the projected 164 runs with a measured number.
- The other five branches (`hist/a`, `c`–`f`), to get an average bisect cost rather than one run.
- Runs per bisect with Culprit's own LLM stages (localiser, fixer, verifier) once they're built.
- Fixed monthly costs and the expected bisects per repo per month. Both are needed before cfo.ai's
  runway and break-even figures mean anything.

## Task 1: v1 → v2 efficiency

- **Staged baseline** (`culprit/baseline.py`): every task runs once on both ends. Only tasks that didn't pass on both ends get the rest of k. Both ends always run the same set of runs, and the Fisher gate counts the runs actually made (a test checks this).
- **Baseline reuse** (`culprit/reuse.py`): results are copied from an earlier run with the same commit SHA, suite SHA, victim provider and model, eval module and k. Each copied row records the run and row it came from. Copied runs aren't charged again, so the budget caps and totals stay correct.
- **Before/after on the fixture** (`scripts/v2_efficiency.py`, `evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md`), victim runs over 4 scenarios:

  | Version | Victim runs | Change vs v1 |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | v1 | 510 | |
  | v2, staged baseline | 430 | −16% |
  | v2, good end reused | 335 | −34% |
  | v2, both ends reused | 270 | −47% |

  All 16 runs found the planted commit, and the bisect steps used the same number of runs in v1 and v2.
- **Real victim (projection only, not measured):** `hist/b` would need about 164 victim runs instead of 240.

## Task 2: M6

- **`culprit report <run_id>`** (`report.py`) writes markdown and a static HTML page. It shows the verdict, the bisect timeline with Wilson intervals against the threshold, skips, intent, diff, trace IDs, costs, and where any reused results came from. I checked the HTML in a browser.
- **`culprit export-costs --format csv`** (`costs.py`) gives per-run cost, victim runs (executed, baseline, bisect, reused) and wall time.
- **`business/cfo-inputs.md`** separates measured, projected and assumed numbers, and labels pricing scenarios A, B and C as hypotheses.

`orchestrator.py` has two small edits: one line now calls the new baseline module, and one saves the intent's source and checkpoint ID for the report. `hackathon.md` and `HOW_IT_WORKS.md` are updated too.

## Before the next paid run
- **v2 on `hist/b` would reuse the whole baseline.** The real ledger already holds run `ff50e3620fdd`, which matches on suite, model and k. A v2 run on `good-v1.0..hist/b` would copy its entire baseline and pay $0 for it. To measure staging on its own, add `--no-reuse`.
- **v1 for comparison:** `--no-reuse --no-staged` gives v1. Runs recorded before v2 resume as v1.
- **Staging has a known blind spot.** It can miss a task that got worse but happened to pass its single run on the bad end. Other tasks that dropped still carry the signal, and this is documented in `baseline.py`.
- **Fixture runs still send neatlogs traces.** I ran the fixture through the CLI, which loads `.env`, so it sent a free trace (`78c72dfa…`).

## 9. Victim agent and seeded benchmark

### 9.1 Victim agent: "RefundDesk"
A customer-support agent that resolves refund requests using **mock tools** backed by a local JSON store:
`lookup_order`, `get_refund_policy`, `issue_refund`, `escalate_to_human`, `send_customer_email`.
The mock layer can inject failures (timeouts, `status: failed` payloads) deterministically per task seed.

**Eval suite:** 20 tasks + 6 held-out tasks. Each task = customer message + initial store state + **deterministic checker** on the final store state and tool-call log (e.g. "refund issued exactly once for ≤ $500", "escalated when order not found", "no refund when lookup failed").

### 9.2 Seeded regressions (ground truth)
Each scenario is a commit range of ~12–16 commits in the separate victim repo, with noise commits (docs, refactors, logging) around one culprit.

| ID | Culprit change | Intended gain | Symptom |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1 (hero)** | "Make it faster": coding agent parallelises tool calls and **removes tool-result validation** | Lower latency | Refunds issued when `lookup_order` failed |
| R2 | Prompt cleanup drops the "> $500 needs escalation" rule | Shorter prompt / cost | Large refunds issued without escalation |
| R3 | Tool schema renames `order_id` → `id` without updating the description | API consistency | Wrong/missing arguments on lookup |
| R4 | `max_retries` 3 → 0 "to reduce latency" | Latency | Fails on flaky-tool tasks |
| R5 | Conversation history window shortened | Token cost | Loses customer details from earlier turns |
| R6 | Lenient JSON parsing of tool calls | Fewer parse errors | Malformed calls executed with defaults |

Plus **one uninstallable commit** (broken dependency pin) placed near the midpoint of at least two scenarios, to exercise skip recovery.

**Honesty rule:** The regressions are deliberately seeded. R1 is created through a real coding-agent session (captured by Entire) given the instruction "make it faster". We say this plainly in the demo and README.

## 10. Verification

A fix is **verified** only if all hold:
1. **Quality:** On full suite + held-out tasks × k, the Wilson interval for `bad+fix` overlaps or exceeds the `good` baseline interval.
2. **Intended gain kept:** The intent metric (latency / tokens / cost, taken from the commit intent) for `bad+fix` is no worse than `bad` by more than a configured tolerance.
3. **No new failures:** No task that passes on `good` fails consistently (all k) on `bad+fix`.

**Benchmark verification of Culprit itself** (`culprit bench`): for each of R1–R6, record whether the culprit commit was correct, whether the hunk was correct, whether the fix verified, victim runs used, cost, wall time. Ground truth is stored in `bench/ground_truth.json` in the Culprit repo (never in the victim repo). Victim history branches use neutral names (`hist/a`…`hist/f`); the scenario mapping lives only in the Culprit repo.

## 11. Failure handling and recovery
## 14. Required tools

### 14.1 neatlogs
- **Tracing:** every victim task run is a trace tagged `commit_sha`, `task_id`, `repetition`, `run_id`. Culprit's own LLM calls are traced separately.
- **Readback:** Task Selector and Localiser pull failing traces via the neatlogs CLI/Public API.
- **Detections:** regex rule on tool results containing `"status": "failed"` followed by `issue_refund`; condition rules such as `cost_usd > <cap>` for runaway runs.
- **Investigate:** used on Culprit **v1** benchmark runs to find why it misidentified or wasted runs.
- **Experiments (prompt versions):** Culprit's Localiser/Task Selector prompts versioned; v1 → v2 promoted by label.
- **Before/after:** `culprit bench --tag v1` and `--tag v2` on the same 6 scenarios. Metrics: culprit accuracy (x/6), hunk accuracy, fix verified (x/6), victim runs per bisect, cost per bisect, wall time. **Numbers are whatever the runs produce; nothing is estimated or rounded in our favour.**

**Instrumentation plan (apply at 12:30, from docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python):**
- Install `pip install -U "neatlogs[anthropic]"` (Python ≥ 3.10, < 3.14). Key from `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in `.env` (gitignored), never hardcoded. Default endpoint `https://ingest.neatlogs.com`.
- Two workflow names, one per entry point: `culprit-bisect` (Culprit CLI `run`/`resume`/`bench`) and `refunddesk-support-agent` (each victim task run, launched as a subprocess in a worktree).
- Capture Anthropic calls with **one** mechanism only: `neatlogs.wrap(Anthropic())` (the docs example uses OpenAI; Anthropic auto-detection is stated, not shown), or `instrumentations=["anthropic"]` with `init()` before the import. Never both.
- `@neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")` on each CLI command and on the victim's task entry point; `kind="TOOL"` on mock tools and on Culprit's git/worktree/eval tools; `kind="AGENT"` on Selector/Localiser/Fixer.
- Per-run metadata via `wrap()` kwargs (`commit_sha`, `task_id`, `repetition`, `run_id`), which become `neatlogs.workflow.<key>`. This is inferred from the docs, so verify in the dashboard.
- Both entry points are one-shot processes, so call `neatlogs.flush()` then `neatlogs.shutdown()` at exit (in `finally`).
- Open: the docs don't show how to read the current trace ID. Ask on Discord or use the CLI/Public API to look traces up by `run_id`/`task_id` metadata.

### 14.2 Entire
- Both repos (`piedpiper-neathacks` = Culprit, `refunddesk` = victim) connected via the Entire GitHub App; `entire enable` in each.
- **Product use:** Culprit reads the culprit commit's session context (`entire checkpoint explain <sha>`) to recover intent.
- **Build use:** every meaningful commit of Culprit is checkpointed; the checkpoint for the v1 → v2 fix is the headline evidence (Sessions → Changes).
- **Trails** (if access granted): the v1 → v2 fix done as a Trail. **Graph** optional.
- Submission includes checkpoint link `https://entire.io/gh/OWNER/REPO/commit/FULL_SHA` and checkpoint ID.

### 14.3 cfo.ai
- **Input:** `culprit export-costs` → Google Sheet (cfo.ai lists Google Sheets as a data connection; fall back to manual upload/entry if the import doesn't work).
- **Measured actuals:** cost per victim run, victim runs per bisect, Culprit LLM cost per bisect, wall time.
- **Pricing scenarios to model** (hypotheses, not facts):
  - **A. Flat SaaS:** $49 / $199 per repo/month with a bisect quota.
  - **B. Customer's own model key + platform fee** (recommended hypothesis): customer pays victim-run LLM cost; we charge a platform fee.
  - **C. Metered:** platform fee + per-bisect charge.
- **Questions for Ari:** gross margin per customer under A vs B at 10/50/200 bisects/month · break-even repos with 2 founders · runway under base/upside/downside acquisition · stress test with a 10× more expensive victim agent.
- **Deliverable:** exported business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) in `/business/` and linked from the README.

## Claude Sonnet 5.5

Only `hist/b` is measured (visible). The rest are not measured.
- **Done: M3 `culprit bench` (branch `feat/bench`, fixture only, $0).**
  - `bench/scenarios.yaml` (six branches, `good-v1.0` → `origin/hist/<x>`) and `bench/ground_truth.json`: full culprit SHAs, branch heads, uninstallable commits (`22a37db`, `2ad118e`), responsible hunks as file + line range from `git show`, and the intended-gain metric. All positions re-checked against `git rev-list` in the RefundDesk clone (read-only).
  - `culprit bench --tag v1|v2` runs each scenario through the normal orchestrator, one after another, and scores it: `correct`, `wrong`, `correct_no_regression`, `missed`, `no_regression_unverified`, `ambiguous_*` or `incomplete`, plus victim runs, cost, wall time, skipped commits, run ID and neatlogs trace IDs. It writes `evidence/bench-<tag>.md` and `.json`.
  - `--score-runs <id,...>` / `--score-latest` score runs already in the ledger, matched to scenarios by their recorded good/bad SHAs, so the paid runs on `hist/*` don't need repeating. Scoring opens the ledger **read-only**, so it is safe while another process is still writing it.
  - Leakage guard: only resolved SHAs reach the orchestrator (no scenario names, no answers); bench refuses ground-truth files inside the victim repo.
  - Fixture bench, 2 scenarios: the planted break was found (`correct`, with the unbuildable commit SKIPped), and a clean range ended `correct_no_regression` (Fisher p = 0.69). Accuracy 2/2, 180 fake runs. 86 tests pass (18 new).

- **Decision:** a `no_regression` result is only scored as correct when ground truth says so: no bug planted in the range, or a measurement on that victim model showed the bug is invisible. Otherwise it's `no_regression_unverified` (not counted as accurate) until the strength check is done. Only `hist/b` has a visibility measurement (GLM 5.3 and Sonnet 5.5: 18/18 → 0/18). Visibility is never taken from a Culprit run's own baselines (that would be Culprit grading itself); it must come from the separate strength check (Prompt G step 4) recorded with run IDs in `bench/strength.md`.
- **Decision:** hist/a ("API consistency") and hist/e ("fewer rejected tool calls") get intended-gain metric `null`, because their claimed gain isn't latency, tokens or cost.

- **Done: `tests/conftest.py`** (committed with bench as `94d0a26`). Every test runs without `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`, with tracing off and with both provider calls blocked, so tests can't export traces or spend money.
- **Done: M5 part 1, the Localiser (PRD §8.3; branch `feat/bench`, fake victim only, $0).**
  - It splits the culprit diff into hunks, leaving out `evals/`, which the pinned suite replaces.
  - One AI call (`llm.structured`) ranks the hunks from the diff, the leak-filtered intent and the telling tasks' results. Its order is stored, so resume never asks twice, and diff order is the fallback if the call fails.
  - It is a separate command, `culprit localise <run_id>`, that reads a finished, found run from the ledger. The orchestrator gained only a step-kind prefix and a filter, because another session is changing it in parallel.
  - It reverse-applies the top 3 hunks one at a time on the culprit commit, each in its own worktree. Each revert is judged by the same Wilson rule, resampling, budget and resume as a bisect step, then pairs are tried (capped at 3), then the answer falls back to the whole commit.
  - **Fake-victim results:**
    - Multi-hunk culprit, with the fake model wrong on purpose (ranking a harmless timeout change first): that revert stayed BAD, the next one flipped the commit to GOOD, and the hunk was named correctly.
    - Culprit that needs two hunks together, with no model available (diff-order fallback): every single revert stayed BAD, and a pair flipped it.
    - Resume reran nothing and made no new model call.
  - 96 tests pass (10 new).
- **Dry check on the real culprit commits** (git archive trees, no victim runs): every hunk of all six commits reverse-applies on its own (9, 16, 3, 1, 6 and 3 hunks).
- **Finding worth posting:** on the hero commit, "revert one hunk at a time" can't work. The retry-loop hunk calls `validate_tool_result`, which another hunk of the same commit deleted, so only the pair restores behaviour. A localiser that stops at single hunks would blame the whole commit.
- **Decision:** reverts are applied on the culprit commit, not on the branch head, so later commits can't block a hunk. The Fixer will work on the head.
- **Not yet:** failing-trace contents from neatlogs in the ranking prompt. The prompt uses the ledger's pass counts, errors and task definitions for now.
- **Moment worth screenshotting:** the fake-victim log, `hunk ranking (llm): h4, h3, h1`, then `localise:h4: 1/15 … → BAD`, then `localise:h3: 14/15 … → GOOD`, then `responsible: hunk 3 (refunddesk/agent.py:3)`.

- **Done: M5 part 2, the Fixer and Verifier (PRD §8.4, §10), as `culprit fix <run_id>`** (fake victim only, $0). Shared run loading moved into `finished.py`, so `localise` and `fix` don't touch the orchestrator.
  - **Fixer:** one AI call per attempt returns the intended gain (latency/tokens/cost/none) and exact search-and-replace edits. Culprit builds the patch itself, and only the responsible hunks' files may change.
  - **Verifier:** runs the full suite plus held-out tasks × k at the bad head with the patch applied. It passes only if quality is restored, the intended gain is kept (10% tolerance) and there are no new always-failing tasks. Failed attempts are fed back; after 2, the responsible hunks' revert is verified instead.
  - **Fake-victim log** (the culprit also made the agent faster):
    - `fix:1: 34/36 … latency 300 vs bad 100; FAILED: intended gain lost`
    - `fix:2: 34/36 … latency 100 vs bad 100; VERIFIED`
    - With no model, both attempts fail and the hunk revert is `verified_revert`.
  - 109 tests pass (13 new).
- **Finding worth posting:** PRD §10's quality gate ("the fix's 95% interval overlaps the good baseline's") is lenient: a fix passing 4/9 against good's 8/9 passes it. The "no task that always passed now always fails" gate is what catches such a fix. A Fisher test, like the regression gate's, would be stricter; candidate for M4.
- **Moment worth screenshotting:** the two `fix:` lines above: the Verifier refusing a fix that quietly gives the speed-up back.

- **Done: v2 efficiency (branch `feat/v2-efficiency`, fixture only, $0).** This is the required before/after.
  - **Staged baseline** (`culprit/baseline.py`): every task ×1 on both ends, then the full k only on tasks that didn't pass on both. Both ends run the same (task, repetition) set, and the Fisher gate uses the runs actually made.
  - **Baseline reuse** (`culprit/reuse.py`): results at a commit are copied from an earlier run with the same commit SHA, suite SHA, victim provider and model, eval module and k.   - Runs recorded before v2 resume as v1. `culprit run --no-reuse --no-staged` gives v1.
- **Done: M6 report and costs.**
  - `culprit report <run_id>` writes markdown plus static HTML: verdict, baselines and gate, bisect timeline with Wilson intervals against the threshold, skips, intent, diff, trace IDs, costs and reuse provenance.

  - `business/cfo-inputs.md` holds the measured and projected unit costs, with pricing scenarios A/B/C labelled as hypotheses.

# Blockers, unsupported features and known discrepancies

Each entry lists what the PRD assumed, what the tool actually supports (sources in `docs/research.md`), and the fallback we chose.

## Known discrepancies

### neatlogs cost for `claude-sonnet-5-5` differs from the list price

- **Observed:** for one call of 131 input and 18 output tokens, neatlogs reported `costUsd = 0.000663` (trace `ffdf497989747bf30856935f187e6013`, LLM span). That matches $3/$15 per MTok.
- **List price:** Anthropic's published list price for `claude-sonnet-5-5` is $2/$10 per MTok (cached 2026-10-06), which gives $0.000442 for the same call.
- **Decision:** Culprit's ledger (`culprit.llm.ANTHROPIC_PRICES`, $2/$10) is the only source of truth for cost, `export-costs` and cfo.ai. neatlogs' cost fields are not used in any cost number. Evidence tables that show neatlogs costs label them "neatlogs-reported, not used".

## Unsupported or changed vs the PRD

| PRD assumption | Reality | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Look up victim traces by `run_id` / `commit_sha` metadata (§14.1) | The read API and CLI can't filter on, or return, custom span attributes | Culprit stores every trace ID in the ledger. Its own traces use `session_id = run_id`, and run context also goes into each span's input JSON so readback can verify it |
| Read the current trace ID in code (§14.1 open question) | No getter in the SDK | `inject_trace_context()` W3C traceparent; verified to equal the read API's `traceId` |
| Investigate on v1 benchmark runs (§14.1) | Dashboard only; no API or CLI | Use Investigate by hand in the dashboard; record findings and screenshots in `evidence/` |
| Detection "`status: failed` followed by `issue_refund`" (§14.1) | Detections are per-span regex or conditional rules; a cross-span sequence can't be expressed in one rule | Not built yet (M4). Plan: regex on `issue_refund` tool spans plus a Culprit-side sequence check |
| `entire checkpoint explain` intent | The `## Intent` field can be a harness event (`<task-notification>`) or `*(no prompt recorded)*`, and `--json` carries no intent | Culprit reads the session's typed prompts from `--transcript` when Intent is a placeholder; commit message and diff when there is no checkpoint |
| OpenRouter provider | Dropped at first, then reinstated as the fallback (Sat evening) | Anthropic (Sonnet 5.5) when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, otherwise OpenRouter (GLM 5.3). Culprit picks the victim model once per run and records it, so all commits are judged by the same model |
## Known limitations and next steps

- Built: M1–M3, M5 (`culprit localise`, `culprit fix`) and M6 (`culprit report`, `export-costs`), plus v2 staged and reused baselines. Not done yet: localise and fix on the real victim, the real v1 vs v2 benchmark, and neatlogs Investigate/Detections. v2's real-victim savings are projected, not measured.

## Submission

Requirements confirmed from https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (read 2026-10-10):

- [ ] Uses neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai (cfo.ai business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, runway)
- [ ] Before/after run of the agent with compared numbers (e.g., two neatlogs traces)

- [ ] Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output
- [ ] A run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next
- [ ] Building-in-public links tagged #neatHack
- [ ] Public repo with commits dated during the hackathon
- [ ] Demo video (the length limit isn't on the page; the PRD says ≤ 3 min, *pending confirmation*)
- [ ] Submit on X by quoting the official neatlogs post with team, name, project, public repo and demo. Window: Mon 12 Oct 2026, 7:00–11:55 PM IST

Judging weights (published): agent 30%, use of neatlogs/Entire/cfo.ai 25%, demo video 20%, building in public 15%, usefulness/originality 10%.
